anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonable, often because of cost-model or plan-reuse issues.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The database engine allocates or leaks memory far beyond the safe limits of the host, triggering paging, OOM events, or cache thrashing.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical pages or index structures on disk have become internally inconsistent, leading to checksum errors, incorrect key ordering, or wrong heap-to-index mappings.

When these three anomalies arise together, operators observe a confusing blend of symptoms: unpredictable plan flips or fallback to full scans are interleaved with sudden memory-pressure spikes as bad plans inflate work buffers, while corrupted indexes return duplicate or missing rows that force the optimizer into even more conservative (and memory-hungry) scan strategies. Concurrently, inflated buffer pools and runaway sorts push the node into swapping, which further slows corruption verification and recovery tasks. Error logs show alternating entries for checksum failures, plan-cache evictions, memory-pressure throttling, and repeated statement re-compilations, making it difficult to attribute performance collapse to any single layer.

Causally, latent page or index corruption can silently distort cardinality feedback, misleading the optimizer toward plans that read or join far more rows than expected; these bloated plans in turn request large hash, sort, or bitmap buffers, accelerating memory exhaustion. As memory pressure mounts, the engine evicts useful pages, intensifies I/O, and heightens the probability of reading the already-corrupted blocks, thereby surfacing more integrity errors. Each plan recompile triggered by corruption or eviction can produce a different sub-optimal plan, multiplying memory demand and worsening the vicious cycle. The intertwined nature of wrong plans, memory over-commitment, and structural corruption therefore amplifies instability, culminating in severe performance degradation, intermittent query failures, and potential node crashes.

entry.error_class: Class HV - Foreign Data Wrapper Error (SQL/MED)
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
